sanskrit: tau samīkṣya tu vitrastāv akṛtārthau pradhāvitau tayoś ca dravator vipraṃ jagṛhe nṛpatir balāt
english: Seeing those two, frightened and having not achieved their purpose, they fled; but as the two ran away, the king seized the brahmin by force.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā gṛhītaṃ bhartāram atha brāhmaṇy abhāṣata śṛṇu rājan vaco mahyaṃ yat tvāṃ vakṣyāmi suvrata
english: Seeing her husband seized, the brahmin woman then spoke: "Listen, O king, to the words I will speak to you, O virtuous one."

sanskrit: ādityavaṃśaprabhavas tvaṃ hi lokapariśrutaḥ apramattaḥ sthito dharme guruśuśrūṣaṇe rataḥ
english: "You are indeed born of the lineage of the Sun, celebrated throughout the world, ever-vigilant, established in righteousness, and devoted to the service of your teacher."

sanskrit: śāpaṃ prāpto 'si durdharṣa na pāpaṃ kartum arhasi ṛtukāle tu saṃprāpte bhartrāsmy adya samāgatā
english: "You have received a curse, O unconquerable one — you ought not to commit sin. The fertile season having arrived, I have today come together with my husband."

sanskrit: akṛtārthā hy ahaṃ bhartrā prasavārthaś ca me mahān prasīda nṛpatiśreṣṭha bhartā me 'yaṃ visṛjyatām
english: "I have not yet attained my purpose with my husband, and my longing for offspring is great. Be pleased, O best of kings — let this husband of mine be released."

sanskrit: evaṃ vikrośamānāyās tasyāḥ sa sunṛśaṃsakṛt bhartāraṃ bhakṣayām āsa vyāghro mṛgam ivepsitam
english: Even as she cried out thus, that doer of terrible deeds devoured her husband as a tiger devours a coveted deer.

sanskrit: tasyāḥ krodhābhibhūtāyā yad aśru nyapatad bhuvi so 'gniḥ samabhavad dīptas taṃ ca deśaṃ vyadīpayat
english: The tears that fell to the ground from her, overcome with rage, became a blazing fire and lit up that very place.

sanskrit: tataḥ sā śokasaṃtaptā bhartṛvyasanaduḥkhitā kalmāṣapādaṃ rājarṣim aśapad brāhmaṇī ruṣā
english: Then she, tormented by grief and afflicted by the calamity of losing her husband, that brahmin woman cursed the royal sage Kalmāṣapāda in fury.

sanskrit: yasmān mamākṛtārthāyās tvayā kṣudra nṛśaṃsavat prekṣantyā bhakṣito me 'dya prabhur bhartā mahāyaśāḥ
english: "Because, O wretch, you have cruelly devoured before my eyes my lord and husband of great glory, while I had not yet achieved my purpose —"

sanskrit: tasmāt tvam api durbuddhe macchāpaparivikṣataḥ patnīm ṛtāv anuprāpya sadyas tyakṣyasi jīvitam
english: "Therefore you too, O evil-minded one, struck by my curse, shall instantly give up your life the moment you approach your wife in her fertile season."

sanskrit: yasya carṣer vasiṣṭhasya tvayā putrā vināśitāḥ tena saṃgamya te bhāryā tanayaṃ janayiṣyati sa te vaṃśakaraḥ putro bhaviṣyati nṛpādhama
english: "The sons of that seer Vasiṣṭha were destroyed by you; having united with him, your wife shall bear a son — that son who perpetuates your lineage shall be born, O most vile of kings."

sanskrit: evaṃ śaptvā tu rājānaṃ sā tam āṅgirasī śubhā tasyaiva saṃnidhau dīptaṃ praviveśa hutāśanam
english: Having thus cursed the king, that auspicious woman of Āṅgirasa descent entered the blazing sacred fire right there in his presence.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭhaś ca mahābhāgaḥ sarvam etad apaśyata jñānayogena mahatā tapasā ca paraṃtapa
english: And the highly blessed Vasiṣṭha witnessed all of this, O scorcher of foes, through the power of great knowledge and his austerities.

sanskrit: muktaśāpaś ca rājarṣiḥ kālena mahatā tataḥ ṛtukāle 'bhipatito madayantyā nivāritaḥ
english: After a great length of time the royal sage was released from the curse; and when at the fertile season he approached Madayantī, he was restrained by her.

sanskrit: na hi sasmāra nṛpatis taṃ śāpaṃ śāpamohitaḥ devyāḥ so 'tha vacaḥ śrutvā sa tasyā nṛpasattamaḥ taṃ ca śāpam anusmṛtya paryatapyad bhṛśaṃ tadā
english: The king, bewildered by the curse, did not recall that curse; but upon hearing the queen's words, that best of kings, recollecting the curse, was then greatly tormented.

sanskrit: etasmāt kāraṇād rājā vasiṣṭhaṃ saṃnyayojayat svadāre bharataśreṣṭha śāpadoṣasamanvitaḥ
english: For this reason the king, afflicted by the fault of the curse, engaged Vasiṣṭha with his own wife, O best of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca asmākam anurūpo vai yaḥ syād gandharva vedavit purohitas tam ācakṣva sarvaṃ hi viditaṃ tava
english: Arjuna said: "Indeed, tell us, O Gandharva, who would be a suitable purohita for us — one learned in the Vedas. All is known to you."

sanskrit: gandharva uvāca yavīyān devalasyaiṣa vane bhrātā tapasyati dhaumya utkocake tīrthe taṃ vṛṇudhvaṃ yadīcchatha
english: The Gandharva said: "The younger brother of Devala practices austerity in the forest — Dhaumya, at the ford called Utkocaka. Choose him if you wish."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato 'rjuno 'stram āgneyaṃ pradadau tad yathāvidhi gandharvāya tadā prīto vacanaṃ cedam abravīt
english: Vaiśampāyana said: Then Arjuna duly gave the Āgneya weapon to the Gandharva, and pleased, spoke these words to him.

sanskrit: tvayy eva tāvat tiṣṭhantu hayā gandharvasattama karmakāle grahīṣyāmi svasti te 'stv iti cābravīt
english: "Let the horses remain with you for now, O best of Gandharvas; I will take them when the time for their use arrives" — and he also said: "May you fare well."

sanskrit: te 'nyonyam abhisaṃpūjya gandharvaḥ pāṇḍavāś ca ha ramyād bhāgīrathīkacchād yathākāmaṃ pratasthire
english: They honoured one another, and then the Gandharva and the Pāṇḍavas departed as they wished from the pleasant bank of the Bhāgīrathī.

sanskrit: tata utkocakaṃ tīrthaṃ gatvā dhaumyāśramaṃ tu te taṃ vavruḥ pāṇḍavā dhaumyaṃ paurohityāya bhārata
english: Then, going to the ford of Utkocaka and to Dhaumya's hermitage, the Pāṇḍavas chose Dhaumya for the office of purohita, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tān dhaumyaḥ pratijagrāha sarvavedavidāṃ varaḥ pādyena phalamūlena paurohityena caiva ha
english: Dhaumya, the foremost among those who know all the Vedas, received them with water for the feet and with fruits and roots, and also took on the office of purohita for them.

sanskrit: te tadāśaṃsire labdhāṃ śriyaṃ rājyaṃ ca pāṇḍavāḥ taṃ brāhmaṇaṃ puraskṛtya pāñcālyāś ca svayaṃvaram
english: Then the Pāṇḍavas, placing that brahmin foremost, hoped to obtain prosperity and kingdom, and also the svayaṃvara of the Pāñcālī.

sanskrit: mātṛṣaṣṭhās tu te tena guruṇā saṃgatās tadā nāthavantam ivātmānaṃ menire bharatarṣabhāḥ
english: Those bulls among the Bharatas, together with their mother — six of them — united with that teacher, then considered themselves as though they had a protector.

sanskrit: sa hi vedārthatattvajñas teṣāṃ gurur udāradhīḥ tena dharmavidā pārthā yājyāḥ sarvavidā kṛtāḥ
english: For that noble-minded one, knowing the true import of the Vedas, became their teacher; by him, who was learned in righteousness and all knowledge, the Pārthas were made fit to be officiated for in sacrifice.

sanskrit: vīrāṃs tu sa hi tān mene prāptarājyān svadharmataḥ buddhivīryabalotsāhair yuktān devān ivāparān
english: He regarded those heroes as having attained kingship by their own duty, endowed with intelligence, heroism, strength, and enterprise — like other gods.

sanskrit: kṛtasvastyayanās tena tatas te manujādhipāḥ menire sahitā gantuṃ pāñcālyās taṃ svayaṃvaram
english: Having had the auspicious rites performed for them by him, those lords of men then resolved together to go to the svayaṃvara of the Pāñcālī.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tatas te naraśārdūlā bhrātaraḥ pañca pāṇḍavāḥ prayayur draupadīṃ draṣṭuṃ taṃ ca devamahotsavam
english: Vaiśampāyana said: Then those five brothers, tigers among men, the Pāṇḍavas, set out to see Draupadī and that great festival equal to the gods.

sanskrit: te prayātā naravyāghrā mātrā saha paraṃtapāḥ brāhmaṇān dadṛśur mārge gacchataḥ sagaṇān bahūn
english: Those tigers among men, scorchers of foes, as they set out together with their mother, saw on the road many brahmins going with their groups.

sanskrit: tān ūcur brāhmaṇā rājan pāṇḍavān brahmacāriṇaḥ kva bhavanto gamiṣyanti kuto vāgacchateti ha
english: The brahmins, O king, spoke to those Pāṇḍavas who appeared as celibate students: "Where are you gentlemen going, and from where have you come?"

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca āgatān ekacakrāyāḥ sodaryān devadarśinaḥ bhavanto hi vijānantu sahitān mātṛcāriṇaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "Know us, O seers of the divine, as brothers come from Ekacakrā, travelling together with our mother."

sanskrit: brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ gacchatādyaiva pāñcālān drupadasya niveśanam svayaṃvaro mahāṃs tatra bhavitā sumahādhanaḥ
english: The brahmins said: "Go today itself to the Pāñcāla lands, to the dwelling of Drupada — a great svayaṃvara with enormous riches will take place there."

sanskrit: ekasārthaṃ prayātāḥ smo vayam apy atra gāminaḥ tatra hy adbhutasaṃkāśo bhavitā sumahotsavaḥ
english: "We too are travelling in the same caravan and heading there; for a great festival of wondrous appearance will take place there."

sanskrit: yajñasenasya duhitā drupadasya mahātmanaḥ vedīmadhyāt samutpannā padmapatranibhekṣaṇā
english: "The daughter of Yajñasena, the great-souled Drupada, born from the midst of the sacrificial altar, her eyes resembling the petals of a lotus —"

sanskrit: darśanīyānavadyāṅgī sukumārī manasvinī dhṛṣṭadyumnasya bhaginī droṇaśatroḥ pratāpinaḥ
english: "— beautiful to behold, with faultless limbs, tender, spirited, the sister of Dhṛṣṭadyumna the powerful, enemy of Droṇa —"

sanskrit: yo jātaḥ kavacī khaḍgī saśaraḥ saśarāsanaḥ susamiddhe mahābāhuḥ pāvake pāvakaprabhaḥ
english: "— who was born, the great-armed one, clad in armour, bearing sword, arrows and bow, from the well-kindled sacred fire, blazing like fire itself —"

sanskrit: svasā tasyānavadyāṅgī draupadī tanumadhyamā nīlotpalasamo gandho yasyāḥ krośāt pravāyati
english: "— the sister of that one, the faultless-limbed Draupadī of slender waist, whose fragrance, equal to that of a blue lotus, wafts from a league away —"

sanskrit: tāṃ yajñasenasya sutāṃ svayaṃvarakṛtakṣaṇām gacchāmahe vayaṃ draṣṭuṃ taṃ ca devamahotsavam
english: "— to see her, the daughter of Yajñasena, for whom the svayaṃvara occasion has been arranged, and that great festival equal to the gods, we are going."

sanskrit: rājāno rājaputrāś ca yajvāno bhūridakṣiṇāḥ svādhyāyavantaḥ śucayo mahātmāno yatavratāḥ
english: "Kings and princes, performers of sacrifice with lavish gifts, devoted to Vedic study, pure, great-souled, firm in their vows —"

sanskrit: taruṇā darśanīyāś ca nānādeśasamāgatāḥ mahārathāḥ kṛtāstrāś ca samupaiṣyanti bhūmipāḥ
english: "— young, handsome, come from various lands, great warriors, skilled in arms — these lords of the earth will assemble there."

sanskrit: te tatra vividhān dāyān vijayārthaṃ nareśvarāḥ pradāsyanti dhanaṃ gāś ca bhakṣyaṃ bhojyaṃ ca sarvaśaḥ
english: "Those lords of men will give there various gifts for the sake of winning — wealth, cows, and all manner of food and provisions."

sanskrit: pratigṛhya ca tat sarvaṃ dṛṣṭvā caiva svayaṃvaram anubhūyotsavaṃ caiva gamiṣyāmo yathepsitam
english: "Having received all of that, and having seen the svayaṃvara, and having enjoyed the festival, we shall go as we desire."

sanskrit: naṭā vaitālikāś caiva nartakāḥ sūtamāgadhāḥ niyodhakāś ca deśebhyaḥ sameṣyanti mahābalāḥ
english: "Actors, bards, dancers, sūtas and māgadhas, and mighty wrestlers will assemble there from various lands."

sanskrit: evaṃ kautūhalaṃ kṛtvā dṛṣṭvā ca pratigṛhya ca sahāsmābhir mahātmānaḥ punaḥ pratinivartsyatha
english: "Having thus gratified your curiosity, and having seen and received gifts, O great-souled ones, you shall return with us."

sanskrit: darśanīyāṃś ca vaḥ sarvān devarūpān avasthitān samīkṣya kṛṣṇā varayet saṃgatyānyatamaṃ varaṃ
english: "And having seen all of you, handsome as gods, as you stand there, Kṛṣṇā might by chance choose one among you as her chosen lord."

sanskrit: ayaṃ bhrātā tava śrīmān darśanīyo mahābhujaḥ niyudhyamāno vijayet saṃgatyā draviṇaṃ bahu
english: "This brother of yours, glorious, handsome, and mighty-armed — competing, he might by chance win great wealth."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca paramaṃ bho gamiṣyāmo draṣṭuṃ devamahotsavam bhavadbhiḥ sahitāḥ sarve kanyāyās taṃ svayaṃvaram
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "Most certainly, sirs, we shall go, all of us together with you, to see that great festival equal to the gods and the svayaṃvara of that maiden."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktāḥ prayātās te pāṇḍavā janamejaya rājñā dakṣiṇapāñcālān drupadenābhirakṣitān
english: Vaiśampāyana said: Thus addressed, the Pāṇḍavas set out, O Janamejaya, to the southern Pāñcāla lands protected by king Drupada.

sanskrit: tatas te taṃ mahātmānaṃ śuddhātmānam akalmaṣam dadṛśuḥ pāṇḍavā rājan pathi dvaipāyanaṃ tadā
english: Then, O king, the Pāṇḍavas saw on the road that great-souled one, the pure-souled and sinless Dvaipāyana.

sanskrit: tasmai yathāvat satkāraṃ kṛtvā tena ca sāntvitāḥ kathānte cābhyanujñātāḥ prayayur drupadakṣayam
english: Having honoured him duly, being comforted by him, and at the end of their conversation receiving his permission, they proceeded to the abode of Drupada.

sanskrit: paśyanto ramaṇīyāni vanāni ca sarāṃsi ca tatra tatra vasantaś ca śanair jagmur mahārathāḥ
english: Beholding the charming forests and lakes, resting here and there, those great warriors went slowly.

sanskrit: svādhyāyavantaḥ śucayo madhurāḥ priyavādinaḥ ānupūrvyeṇa saṃprāptāḥ pāñcālān kurunandanāḥ
english: Devoted to Vedic study, pure, gentle and sweet-spoken, the Kuru princes arrived in due order in the Pāñcāla country.

sanskrit: te tu dṛṣṭvā puraṃ tac ca skandhāvāraṃ ca pāṇḍavāḥ kumbhakārasya śālāyāṃ niveśaṃ cakrire tadā
english: The Pāṇḍavas, having seen the city and the encampment, then took up lodging in the workshop of a potter.

sanskrit: tatra bhaikṣaṃ samājahrur brāhmīṃ vṛttiṃ samāśritāḥ tāṃś ca prāptāṃs tadā vīrāñ jajñire na narāḥ kva cit
english: There they collected alms, living by the way of a brahmin; no one anywhere recognised those heroes who had arrived.

sanskrit: yajñasenasya kāmas tu pāṇḍavāya kirīṭine kṛṣṇāṃ dadyām iti sadā na caitad vivṛṇoti saḥ
english: But the wish of Yajñasena was always: "May I give Kṛṣṇā to the Pāṇḍava, the diadem-wearer" — yet he did not reveal this.

sanskrit: so 'nveṣamāṇaḥ kaunteyān pāñcālyo janamejaya dṛḍhaṃ dhanur anāyamyaṃ kārayām āsa bhārata
english: The Pāñcāla king, O Janamejaya, O Bhārata, searching for the Kaunteyās, had a mighty bow made that was impossible to string.

sanskrit: yantraṃ vaihāyasaṃ cāpi kārayām āsa kṛtrimam tena yantreṇa sahitaṃ rājā lakṣyaṃ ca kāñcanam
english: He also had made an artificial machine in the sky, and along with that machine the king had a golden target made.

sanskrit: drupada uvāca idaṃ sajyaṃ dhanuḥ kṛtvā sajyenānena sāyakaiḥ atītya lakṣyaṃ yo veddhā sa labdhā matsutām iti
english: Drupada said: "He who, having strung this bow and with these arrows from it, passes through the machine and strikes the target — he shall win my daughter."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca iti sa drupado rājā sarvataḥ samaghoṣayat tac chrutvā pārthivāḥ sarve samīyus tatra bhārata
english: Vaiśampāyana said: Thus king Drupada had it proclaimed everywhere; hearing it, all the kings, O Bhārata, gathered there.

sanskrit: ṛṣayaś ca mahātmānaḥ svayaṃvaradidṛkṣayā duryodhanapurogāś ca sakarṇāḥ kuravo nṛpa
english: And great-souled sages, wishing to witness the svayaṃvara, as well as the Kurus headed by Duryodhana and accompanied by Karṇa, O king —

sanskrit: brāhmaṇāś ca mahābhāgā deśebhyaḥ samupāgaman te 'bhyarcitā rājagaṇā drupadena mahātmanā
english: — and greatly blessed brahmins came from various lands; those groups of kings were honoured by the great-souled Drupada.

sanskrit: tataḥ paurajanāḥ sarve sāgaroddhūtaniḥsvanāḥ śiśumārapuraṃ prāpya nyaviśaṃs te ca pārthivāḥ
english: Then all the townsfolk, with a roar like that raised by the ocean, reached the city of Śiśumāra; those kings too took up residence there.

sanskrit: prāguttareṇa nagarād bhūmibhāge same śubhe samājavāṭaḥ śuśubhe bhavanaiḥ sarvato vṛtaḥ
english: To the northeast of the city, on a level and auspicious plot of ground, the festival arena shone, surrounded on all sides by pavilions.

sanskrit: prākāraparikhopeto dvāratoraṇamaṇḍitaḥ vitānena vicitreṇa sarvataḥ samavastṛtaḥ
english: Enclosed with a wall and moat, adorned with gate-arches, covered everywhere with a variegated canopy —

sanskrit: tūryaughaśatasaṃkīrṇaḥ parārdhyāgurudhūpitaḥ candanodakasiktaś ca mālyadāmaiś ca śobhitaḥ
english: — filled with hundreds of bands of musical instruments, perfumed with the finest aguru incense, sprinkled with sandalwood water, and adorned with garlands and festoons —

sanskrit: kailāsaśikharaprakhyair nabhastalavilekhibhiḥ sarvataḥ saṃvṛtair naddhaḥ prāsādaiḥ sukṛtocchritaiḥ
english: — firmly built, enclosed on all sides with well-constructed tall palaces that resembled the peaks of mount Kailāsa and scraped the sky —

sanskrit: suvarṇajālasaṃvītair maṇikuṭṭimabhūṣitaiḥ sukhārohaṇasopānair mahāsanaparicchadaiḥ
english: — covered with golden lattice-work, adorned with gem-set floors, with stairs easy to ascend, furnished with great seats and coverings —

sanskrit: agrāmyasamavacchannair agurūttamavāsitaiḥ haṃsācchavarṇair bahubhiḥ āyojanasugandhibhiḥ
english: — spread with garments fit for the non-rustic, fragrant with the finest aguru, white as swans, many of them, their perfume carrying for leagues —

sanskrit: asaṃbādhaśatadvāraiḥ śayanāsanaśobhitaiḥ bahudhātupinaddhāṅgair himavacchikharair iva
english: — with hundreds of unobstructed doors, beautified with beds and seats, their bodies studded with many minerals — like the peaks of the Himālaya —

sanskrit: tatra nānāprakāreṣu vimāneṣu svalaṃkṛtāḥ spardhamānās tadānyonyaṃ niṣeduḥ sarvapārthivāḥ
english: There all the kings, splendidly adorned, vying with one another, took their seats in the various kinds of royal pavilions.

sanskrit: tatropaviṣṭān dadṛśur mahāsattvaparākramān rājasiṃhān mahābhāgān kṛṣṇāguruvibhūṣitān
english: There they saw seated those lions among kings, of great spirit and valour, greatly blessed, adorned with black aguru paste.

sanskrit: mahāprasādān brahmaṇyān svarāṣṭraparirakṣiṇaḥ priyān sarvasya lokasya sukṛtaiḥ karmabhiḥ śubhaiḥ
english: Greatly gracious, devoted to the brahmins, protectors of their own kingdoms, dear to all the world through their good deeds and auspicious actions.

sanskrit: mañceṣu ca parārdhyeṣu paurajānapadā janāḥ kṛṣṇādarśanatuṣṭyarthaṃ sarvataḥ samupāviśan
english: On the most excellent galleries the townspeople and country-folk sat down everywhere, eager for the delight of seeing Kṛṣṇā.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇais te ca sahitāḥ pāṇḍavāḥ samupāviśan ṛddhiṃ pāñcālarājasya paśyantas tām anuttamām
english: The Pāṇḍavas too, together with the brahmins, sat down, beholding the unsurpassed prosperity of the king of Pāñcāla.

sanskrit: tataḥ samājo vavṛdhe sa rājan divasān bahūn ratnapradānabahulaḥ śobhito naṭanartakaiḥ
english: Then that assembly grew, O king, over many days, filled with the giving of gems, and beautified by actors and dancers.

sanskrit: vartamāne samāje tu ramaṇīye 'hni ṣoḍaśe āplutāṅgī suvasanā sarvābharaṇabhūṣitā
english: While the assembly was in progress, on the charming sixteenth day, having bathed, dressed in fine garments, adorned with all ornaments —

sanskrit: vīrakāṃsyam upādāya kāñcanaṃ samalaṃkṛtam avatīrṇā tato raṅgaṃ draupadī bharatarṣabha
english: — taking up the hero's bronze vessel that was ornamented with gold, Draupadī then descended into the arena, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: purohitaḥ somakānāṃ mantravid brāhmaṇaḥ śuciḥ paristīrya juhāvāgnim ājyena vidhinā tadā
english: The purohita of the Somakas, a brahmin learned in mantras, pure, having spread the ritual grass, then poured oblations of clarified butter into the fire according to the rite.

sanskrit: sa tarpayitvā jvalanaṃ brāhmaṇān svasti vācya ca vārayām āsa sarvāṇi vāditrāṇi samantataḥ
english: He, having satisfied the blazing fire and having pronounced blessings upon the brahmins, then caused all the musical instruments on every side to cease.
